title: Completed local rings are unchanged by base change to the completed base
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $s\in S$, put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, and let $\widehat A$ be its maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$ lie over $s$. Put $X_B=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $b$ be the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$. There is a unique point $x_B$ above $(x,b)$, and the canonical local base-change map induces an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X_B,x_B}$ as $\widehat A$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, first paragraph (the point x_σ and completed-local identification); algebra.tex Tag 00MA(3) for completion of finite modules and localization calculation

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods S_0=Spec R of s and X_0=Spec C of x with C a finitely generated R-algebra. Writing p subset R and q subset C for the corresponding primes, the local rings are A=R_p and O_{X,x}=C_q. By the fibre-product point correspondence, points above (x,b) correspond to primes of kappa(q) tensor_{kappa(s)} kappa(b). The completion-local-ring statement identifies kappa(b) with kappa(s); hence this tensor product is kappa(q), a field, and there is exactly one point x_B above (x,b). The residue field of x_B is kappa(q).

source.place: Tag 01JT point correspondence, together with Algebra Tag 00MA and the completion-local residue-field clause

proof.text: The completion A^ is Noetherian, local, and has maximal ideal m_A A^ with residue field kappa(s), by the completion Noetherianity and local-completion nodes. The canonical map A \to A^ is flat by the Noetherian-completion-flat node. Base-changing the finite-type affine chart gives D=C tensor_R A^, and localizing at x_B gives D_Q; the induced map C_q \to D_Q is the canonical local base-change map.

source.place: Tags 05GI and 00MB, with the affine base-change construction in Tag 0GDX

proof.text: For every n>=1, the finite-type localization quotient lemma gives a canonical isomorphism C_q/(q C_q)^n \to D_Q/(Q D_Q)^n, and these isomorphisms commute with the transition maps. Applying the compatible inverse-limit lemma to this system yields a canonical isomorphism lim_n C_q/(q C_q)^n \to lim_n D_Q/(Q D_Q)^n. By the definition of adic completion, this is an isomorphism O^_{X,x} \to O^_{X_B,x_B}.

source.place: Tag 00MA(3), finite-module completion and compatible inverse-limit construction

proof.text: The quotient comparison is induced at every level by the canonical local map C_q \to D_Q, so its inverse-limit map is the canonical local base-change map. Naturality of localization and of the quotient projections makes it independent of the affine charts, and the isomorphism is an isomorphism of A^-algebras.
